messages:
anya: Quick sync — we're planning an event-log shape change next week. Goal: remove `actor_email`, add `actor_id_hash` (pseudonymous), and introduce optional `request_origin` tag for client routing info. Need to align on versioning, customer samples, and KMS impacts. ping @mike @liz

mike: Ack. Is the intention to treat `actor_id_hash` as stable across devices? thinking about RBAC lookups that rely on actor identity.

liz: Prefer stable per-account hash (salted via KMS) so we can keep RBAC lookups deterministic without exposing email. That implies KMS tie-in for the salt key rotation story.

anya: Agreed re: stable per-account. Proposal: v2 event envelope where `actor_email` is deprecated but present for 30 days behind a feature flag for customer migration. After 30 days we strip it. Customers get a sample export and a validator tool.

mike: Sounds fine. What about clients that validate schema strictly? we should publish a validation shim lib and a small migration checklist for SDKs.

dana: I'll own the customer-facing migration pack: sample payloads, rolling cutover timeline, and a script to map old fields to the hash so customers can test. ETA Tue.

security-bot: New draft schema uploaded: https://files.redwood.local/schemas/event-envelope-v2-draft.json (internal). Changes highlighted.

liz: KMS questions: how do we rotate the salt without breaking hashes? options: versioned-salt per-account (store salt_version with event) OR include key_id in envelope. Both need careful key-rotation docs. Thoughts?

mike: Prefer including `salt_version` integer on the actor object. That way we can rotate and re-hash new events while old events keep earlier salt. SDKs can accept both and try current salt then fall back.

anya: Good. We'll add `actor:{ id_hash, salt_version }` to v2. For KMS: we should recommend HSM-backed key for production, but allow a customer-managed KMS integration. Add KMS FAQ.

dana: Timeline proposal: alpha in staging Wed, opt-in customers invited Thu, feature-flagged roll for internal services Fri, public deprecation notice on Mon. Customers have 30 days to opt-out of stripping `actor_email`.

mike: Add compatibility test: run consumer adapters against both v1 and v2 for 48h in prod traffic shadowing. Any failing consumers get labeled and owners paged.

liz: Also need RBAC whitelist mapping doc — how to map existing identity asserts (email) to id_hash for access control. I'll draft mapping SQL + rehydration script.

anya: For validation we will provide: (1) sample exports with 1000 events; (2) a small `validate_event_shape` CLI that checks required fields and KMS salt headers; (3) an example CloudWatch/Datadog dashboard for detecting missing `actor.id_hash` occurrences.

dana: I'll stitch the sample export and validator into the migration pack. Also including an example `server-side` shim to translate v1 -> v2 for legacy consumers.

mike: One more: telemetry. Add a metric `events.v2.ingested` and `events.missing_actor_hash` + alert at >0.1% of traffic for 24h. Ops needs that onboarded.

anya: I'll file the ops runbook and incident playbook updates after alpha. For legal/compliance: @liz, can you confirm pseudonymization meets audit requirements for EU customers?

liz: I'll loop in compliance. My read: salted hash with customer-specific salt and key management should be acceptable but will get formal signoff.

mike: Ok — next actions: dana (migration pack + samples), liz (RBAC mapping + compliance check), anya (feature flag + runbook), me (compat tests and metrics). We'll reconvene Fri 10am. :calendar:

anya: Thanks. If anyone spots blockers for KMS integrations (service accounts, IAM perms) drop them here so we can escalate. :thumbsup:
